_comment: Authored analysis: ownership, lifecycle, refcount and locking judgements that no composer can derive, keyed to the C entities they describe. The structural half of each record (field layout, signatures, footprints, casts) is composed from the CodeQL tables on demand and merged in at read time, so a re-extract rewrites nothing here. Written only by `crustify-oracle <target> query {types,symbols} --update`; read through crustify.manifests. Hand-edit at your own risk: `--update` validates a submission against the composed skeleton (unknown field, wrong kind, ptr-invariant violation) and this file does not.

ptr.note: AVAudioFifo owns the av_calloc-allocated table and every AVFifo element. av_audio_fifo_free releases each non-null element through av_fifo_freep2, then releases and nulls the table through av_freep. The field may be NULL during failed construction, and the table and FIFO contents are mutated by allocation, read/write, grow, drain, and reset operations. It is an array of owned pointers, with nb_buffers supplying its element count.

types.name: AVBPrint
types._comment_agent: AVBPrint is a caller-owned, address-sensitive by-value header: av_bprint_init points str into its own reserved_internal_buffer until growth, while av_bprint_init_for_buffer points it into caller storage and growth may replace the internal pointer with an owned av_realloc allocation. av_bprint_finalize releases or transfers only a dynamic allocation and retains the header; moving an initialized header while str selects the internal buffer invalidates the self-pointer, so the type must not be offered through a movable inline owner.

ptr.note: Runtime-conditional string storage: it borrows the enclosing header's reserved_internal_buffer after av_bprint_init, borrows caller storage after av_bprint_init_for_buffer, or owns an av_realloc allocation after growth. It is writable and NUL-terminated while the print buffer is usable. av_bprint_finalize sets an allocated str to NULL when freeing or transferring it, so NULL is reachable in the retained finalized header. The structured lifetime uses 'other' because one slot cannot encode the two borrowed sources (self and the external buffer).

types.name: AVBuffer
types._comment_agent: AVBuffer is public only as an opaque identity behind AVBufferRef. Its internal data allocation is released by the stored callback at the last reference; opaque is runtime-polymorphic callback state and may either be transferred to that callback or borrowed until it runs; free is installed to a non-null static callback on construction. No independent AVBuffer storage dropper is valid because pool entries embed the object.

ptr.note: Byte array of size bytes. av_buffer_create transfers it to the AVBuffer; the stored free callback receives it when the last AVBufferRef is released.
Construction replaces NULL with av_buffer_default_free, so every initialized AVBuffer holds a static code pointer invoked at the last reference.

Type-erased callback state retained until free runs. The callback contract is runtime-polymorphic: callers may transfer context for the callback to dispose or retain externally owned state through the callback.

types.name: AVBufferRef
types._comment_agent: buffer_create initializes both pointers; av_buffer_ref copies the header and increments buffer->refcount; buffer_replace/av_buffer_unref free the reference header and release the underlying buffer on the last count. data is a borrowed window whose extent is size and whose storage lifetime is kept by buffer. The window is ALLOCATED, not written: av_buffer_alloc returns raw av_malloc storage and av_buffer_realloc leaves the region it grows into unwritten, so only av_buffer_allocz (memset) and av_buffer_make_writable (memcpy) hand back a fully initialized one.

ptr.note: This AVBufferRef owns one reference-count unit to the underlying AVBuffer. av_buffer_unref drops that unit; AVBuffer internals including the atomic refcount are mutated through the pointer.

Points at a size-byte window into the allocation kept alive by buffer; references may select different subranges. It can be NULL for an empty/user-supplied zero-size buffer and is writable only under AVBuffer's public writability convention. The window's bytes are allocated but not necessarily initialized: av_buffer_alloc hands back raw av_malloc storage and av_buffer_realloc's growth tail is av_realloc storage, so a consumer may only read bytes some producer wrote.

types.name: AVChannelCustom
types._comment_agent: The opaque field has no libavutil toucher. Custom maps are calloc'd, byte-copied by av_channel_layout_copy, and freed as arrays without per-element disposal, proving this cookie is borrowed and application-managed. The name array is read as a C string by av_channel_layout_index_from_string (strcmp), av_channel_layout_describe_bprint (%s) and av_channel_layout_retype (av_strlcpy), so at most 15 payload bytes are usable and the field must be NUL-terminated or all-zero. channel_layout.h makes sizeof(AVChannelCustom) part of the public ABI, so the element stride is a compatibility property rather than an internal detail.

ptr.note: Application-owned, type-erased private data. libavutil never dereferences or frees it; av_channel_layout_copy copies the pointer value with the map, so the application must keep any pointee alive for every copied layout that retains it.

types.name: AVChannelLayout
types._comment_agent: The order field discriminates u. NATIVE and AMBISONIC use the mask; CUSTOM owns the map; UNSPEC leaves u undefined. The opaque cookie is external application state and survives libavutil layout copies by address only. sizeof(AVChannelLayout) is public ABI, so a by-value owner is the correct Rust representation and av_channel_layout_uninit is its disposer.

ptr.note: Application-managed type-erased cookie. Libavutil preserves and copies the address but never dereferences or frees it; its lifetime must cover every layout copy retaining it.

When order is CUSTOM, the layout owns an nb_channels-element AVChannelCustom array allocated by libavutil and released by av_channel_layout_uninit. Other union variants do not carry a live map. Ownership is EXCLUSIVE: two layouts must never hold the same map, since uninit frees it. C keeps that true even when it fails: av_channel_layout_copy assigns *dst = *src (map pointer included) but stores the refused av_malloc_array result into dst->u.map before testing it, so a failed destination is CUSTOM with a NULL map, not one aliasing the source; the same holds for the av_calloc failure in av_channel_layout_from_string's ambisonic branch. NULL is therefore reachable under CUSTOM, but it is only DISPOSABLE, not READABLE: av_channel_layout_check is the sole reader that tests the pointer (answering 0), while channel_from_index, index_from_channel, index_from_string, describe_bprint, ambisonic_order, masked_description, has_channel_names, retype and copy all walk u.map[i] for i < nb_channels unguarded. A safe wrapper over a CUSTOM layout must exclude NULL whenever nb_channels > 0; nb_channels is the element count, not a capacity, and is non-negative under CUSTOM.

types.name: AVDictionary
types._comment_agent: AVDictionary owns its elems array and the strings held by its inline entries; av_dict_free tears down that complete graph. Reviewed 2026-08-23: the header itself is not stable across a mutation. av_dict_set av_mallocz-es it on the first insertion and av_freep-s it, storing NULL back into the caller slot, once the last entry is removed, so every mutating entry point takes AVDictionary ** rather than AVDictionary *. A nullable owner slot, not a non-null handle, is the only faithful representation.

ptr.note: elems is the dictionary-owned growable array of count inline AVDictionaryEntry values. av_dict_set reallocates and writes it; an empty dictionary may hold NULL; av_dict_free releases every entry key/value and then the array.

types.name: AVDictionaryEntry

ptr.note: Every live entry owns one av_malloc-family NUL-terminated key. av_dict_set rejects NULL or allocation failure before insertion; no observed path writes through a stored key pointer. The containing dictionary frees it, and published borrowed entries forbid caller mutation.

types.name: AVFilmGrainParams
types._comment_agent: Reviewed the complete public layout and film_grain_params.c: all fields are scalars, open-enum values, or a tagged by-value union; there are no pointer, refcount, lock, or separately owned-resource fields. Independent storage comes from av_mallocz and is released as one block with av_free; frame side-data storage is borrowed from the frame.

types.name: AVFrame
types._comment_agent: AVFrame owns its reference headers, side-data collection, dictionaries, channel-layout resources, and conditional pointer tables; plane addresses borrow storage kept alive either by those buffer references or by caller-managed non-refcounted storage. private_ref is an internal RefStruct owner and opaque is application-borrowed identity only. The type has two phases that the pointer fields alone do not express. While it holds no plane and no buffer reference — the state get_frame_defaults (frame.c:31) builds and every av_frame_unref (frame.c:496) restores — the geometry scalars format/width/height/nb_samples/linesize and ch_layout constrain nothing, and av_frame_get_buffer (frame.c:203) allocates from whatever it then reads. Once planes are installed the same scalars describe their extent and every reader takes them on trust. linesize is the one geometry scalar C also accepts from the caller in the first phase: get_video_buffer computes strides only when linesize[0] is zero (frame.c:91), av_image_fill_plane_sizes sizes the allocation from the stride, and av_image_copy2 derives each row's byte width from width, so a supplied stride below the row width is an allocation the next av_frame_copy overruns. C validates only overflow, never the stride against the geometry.

ptr.note: Each non-null slot in the inline eight-element array owns one independently releasable AVBufferRef header; av_frame_unref consumes all slots. Non-null entries must be contiguous.

Each inline slot is an optional interior plane pointer. In a reference-counted frame it borrows storage kept alive by buf/extended_buf; a non-refcounted frame may instead borrow caller-managed storage. Plane extent is a relation with the geometry scalars, not a property of this field: format, width, height and linesize for video; format, nb_samples, ch_layout and linesize[0] for audio. No C reader re-derives it. av_frame_copy (frame.c:711) checks only dst->format == src->format and, in frame_copy_video (frame.c:668), dst->width/height >= src->width/height, then copies src->height rows of av_image_get_linesize(format, src->width) bytes through data at the recorded strides; av_frame_make_writable (frame.c:552) allocates a replacement from the declared geometry and copies into it the same way. Changing a geometry scalar under installed planes therefore overruns the allocation with no further validation.
Owns an av_malloc-family nb_extended_buf-element pointer table and every non-null AVBufferRef header stored in it; av_frame_unref releases headers then table.

Points either at the inline data array (no separate allocation) or at a frame-owned pointer table sized by the audio channel count. Its element plane addresses borrow buffer-backed or caller-managed data; unref frees only a separate table.

Optional owned AVBufferRef header; av_frame_copy_props takes a new reference to it and av_frame_unref consumes it. Not an interchangeable buffer reference: every consumer casts buf->data to FFHWFramesContext and calls through the backend table it finds there — av_hwframe_transfer_data at hwcontext.c:488-490, av_hwframe_get_buffer at hwcontext.c:508, transfer_data_alloc at hwcontext.c:406 — and av_frame_copy (frame.c:678) routes any frame carrying one into that path. It is also paired with the frame's planes, which are opaque surface handles from this context rather than addressable rows; av_hwframe_get_buffer installs both together (hwcontext.c:518, 570), so neither installing one onto a software frame nor clearing one from a hardware frame leaves a frame any reader survives.
Optional frame-owned dictionary, copied by frame property-copy operations and consumed by av_dict_free during unref/replacement.
Application-owned type-erased cookie. Frame operations copy or clear the address but never dereference or free it; the application must keep it alive across every copied frame retaining it.
Optional owned AVBufferRef header carrying reference-counted opaque data; copied with av_buffer_ref and consumed during av_frame_unref.
Internal nullable RefStruct reference owned by one libav* library and consumed by av_refstruct_unref. Public users are forbidden to inspect or change it.
Owns an nb_side_data-element allocated pointer table and every non-null AVFrameSideData entry. av_frame_side_data_free releases entries and table.

The buf owner keeps the data window alive; metadata is a separate nullable owner.

ptr.note: A valid side-data entry owns one independently releasable AVBufferRef header. free_side_data_entry consumes it with av_buffer_unref; mutation of its bytes additionally requires av_buffer_is_writable.

A size-byte window into storage kept alive by buf, potentially at an interior offset. It is not independently freed; mutable access requires the backing AVBufferRef to be writable. The window is ALLOCATED, NOT WRITTEN: av_frame_new_side_data (frame.c) and av_frame_side_data_new (side_data.c) both size it with av_buffer_alloc, i.e. raw av_malloc storage, so a consumer may not present these bytes as initialised until a producer (memcpy in frame_copy_props, av_frame_side_data_clone, or the caller itself) has filled them.
Optional dictionary owned by the side-data entry and consumed by av_dict_free when the entry is replaced or destroyed.

types.name: AVOptionArrayDef
types._comment_agent: AVOptionArrayDef has no lifecycle operation. Its def slot is nullable borrowed read-only static string metadata, not an av_malloc-family owner. Reviewed 2026-08-23: no C code writes any field of this struct. Every definition in the tree is a static const initializer (libavutil/iamf.c, libavutil/tests/opt.c, libavfilter/af_aformat.c, libavfilter/vf_dnn_detect.c) and all six touchers in libavutil/opt.c only read: av_opt_set_array/opt_set_array read size_min and size_max, opt_array_sep reads sep, and av_opt_is_set_to_default/av_opt_set_defaults2/log_default read def. It is never embedded by value either -- AVOption reaches it only by pointer through default_val.arr. opt.h additionally marks def as native access only, leaving size_min, size_max and sep as the foreign-readable members; that is an API-stability contract, not a memory-safety one.

ptr.note: AVClass option is required to be a static AVOption array, and every AVOptionArrayDef initializer is static; its optional def is always a string literal. The struct never frees or mutates the NUL-terminated pointee, and consumers only read it through strlen/strcmp/logging.

types.name: AVOptionRange
types._comment_agent: AVOptionRange has by-value numeric fields and one optional owned string. Default ranges leave str null; custom AVClass.query_ranges callbacks may populate it, and the published av_opt_freep_ranges lifecycle unconditionally releases it with av_freep.

ptr.note: Optional NUL-terminated av_malloc-family string owned by this range. av_opt_freep_ranges releases every non-null range->str with av_freep before freeing the range; the public callback contract returns ranges through that same disposer. The const pointee is read-only.

types.name: AVOptionRanges
types._comment_agent: AVOptionRanges owns its pointer table and every non-null AVOptionRange reached through it. The public av_opt_freep_ranges routine is the sole aggregate destructor and also nulls the caller's slot.

ptr.note: Owned array of AVOptionRange pointers with nb_ranges * nb_components slots. Each non-null element is separately owned by AVOptionRanges; av_opt_freep_ranges frees each element's string and allocation, then the pointer array. types.name: AVPixFmtDescriptor
types._comment_agent: AVPixFmtDescriptor has no allocator, releaser, disposer, or cloner. Nothing in the target writes any field of a descriptor, in the table or elsewhere. nb_components is a cardinality field, not just data: every reader that takes a descriptor pointer (av_get_bits_per_pixel, av_pix_fmt_count_planes, get_pix_fmt_depth, av_image_fill_linesizes, image_copy) walks comp[c] for c < nb_components over an array of exactly 4, and none of them validates the count, so a wrapper must bound it at 4. av_get_bits_per_pixel additionally shifts an int by log2_chroma_w + log2_chroma_h and accumulates comp[c].depth into it, which no per-field bound makes total; a caller-built descriptor is therefore not a safe argument to a descriptor-taking reader, only a table entry is.

free consumes a malloc-family allocation; the allocation may hold a singleton, a counted byte/element buffer, or a NUL-terminated string, and NULL is accepted. mutable is null, not false: free is an external symbol with no definition in this extraction, so no body inspection can decide it -- and it is not observably read-only either, since a real allocator writes its own bookkeeping into the released block. Sole caller in scope is av_free, which forwards ptr unchanged and inherits the same shape. INITIALISATION EXTENT: free places NO initialisation requirement on the block. It releases storage and never reads a value out of it, so the scalar/array/string shapes above say what an allocation MAY hold, not what it DOES hold at the moment of release; that is why all three arms can share one dropper. The requirement lives on the OWNER instead, and this is where malloc and av_memdup part company: a bare malloc return is entirely unwritten -- unlike av_malloc it has not even a CONFIG_MEMORY_POISONING memset to point at -- so it does not yet hold count values of any element type, and a counted typed owner over it is invalid before any view is taken. Such a buffer must be adopted through an uninitialised tier and promoted once filled; only the erased singleton and the already-NUL-terminated string arms can adopt fresh storage as it stands. ZERO SIZE: malloc(0) is implementation-defined and may return NULL, which is indistinguishable from the OOM NULL and is rejected at the wrapper seam anyway; on this campaign's glibc it instead returns a unique live block, measured at 1 byte by LeakSanitizer. So a zero-length owner still owns storage and its release must NOT short-circuit on a zero byte length the way munmap's does -- a guard there leaks, demonstrated by injecting one and watching LSan report the byte. This differs from av_malloc only in mechanism (av_malloc explicitly retries at one byte, malloc's minimum block is the allocator's), not in consequence.

munmap consumes a whole mapped byte range; its separate size argument supplies the extent, so the pointer is array-shaped only and never a singleton or a string. Sole caller in scope is av_file_unmap, which returns early unless bufptr is non-null AND size is non-zero, so the range handed over is always a complete, non-empty MAP_PRIVATE mapping produced by av_file_map's mmap(NULL, size, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE, fd, 0); the release is page-granular, covering ceil(size/pagesize) bytes. mutable is null, not false: munmap is an external symbol with no definition in this extraction, so no body inspection can decide it.
